title: Welcome to Zillow Preferred

slides.title: Your Day 1 workspace
slides.lead: Stay in TrueHQ. Today’s Follow Up Boss practice happens in this session.
slides.body:
Your workspace today

Keep your assigned live session open in your own TrueHQ login. Use the simulated contacts here for every exercise.

First, a walkthrough

We will review how to find a contact using a People-list image. The practice exercises then open directly inside a fictional contact record.

Then, your turn

When your presenter opens an activity, complete it on your own screen. Save the changes and check your work here. You do not need to open Follow Up Boss or find a real client.
slides.notes: Before class, create the Day 1 session using the updated lesson. Confirm each selected learner can join through their own TrueHQ login. Keep the presenter console private and share the presentation window. Explain the team’s actual lead routing verbally: a live buyer connection, tour request, and touring alert are different events; a request alone is not an appointment. Then use the on-screen references and simulator throughout. Do not send learners to a separate Follow Up Boss account. Watching the presenter is not completing an individual exercise.
slides.cue: Can everyone see this session in their own TrueHQ account?

slides.title: Start in People
slides.lead: The full People reference is open below. Review the controls together, then continue here.
slides.notes: Stay in TrueHQ. The full reference image is already displayed on this page; scroll to inspect its controls. Point out People, search, smart lists, and filtering. Ask learners which controls they would use and how they would confirm the source and recent activity. This is a walkthrough, not a completed search task. The simulator begins inside a contact; no external account is needed for class.
slides.cue: Which control would you use to find a contact by name?

slides.title: Explain how you would find Avery
slides.lead: Use the People-list reference. Describe your path without leaving this session.

Locate the name

Confirm the source

Explain where you would check for Zillow and when you would use a Lead Source filter.

Check before editing

Describe how you would confirm the name, assignment, and recent activity. The next practice exercise opens the fictional record for you.
slides.notes: Open the written activity and have every learner submit their own navigation explanation in TrueHQ. Ask one learner to talk through the image, then clarify missed controls. Do not require a search in a separate training pond. This response shows navigation understanding, not verified hands-on search. If needed, arrange a separate coach-observed navigation check in the team’s Follow Up Boss training account after class; it is not a prerequisite for today’s simulated record exercises.
slides.cue: Explain the path you would take, then submit your own answer here.

slides.title: Write what the next agent needs
slides.lead: Record what happened, what the buyer said, and the agreed next step.
slides.body:
“Spoke with Avery. Looking for three bedrooms in Tacoma in 60–90 days. I’ll send two homes on Thursday, then call to compare them.”

Keep the facts

Use the buyer’s words where they clarify a need.

Make the next step specific

Name the action and agreed date.

Leave out guesses

A friendly conversation is not proof of readiness or budget.
slides.notes: Ask what the example tells the next caller. Then complete the note exercise. Coach one missing fact rather than rewriting the entire note for the agent. Keep source, assignment, and history in view. Background information suggests a question; it does not establish finances, family circumstances, timing, or readiness. The note check measures saving an action, not writing quality.
slides.cue: Could someone follow up using only this note?

slides.title: Give the follow-up a date and time
slides.lead: Write an action you will recognize when it comes due.
slides.body:
History versus next action

The note says what happened. The task schedules what happens next.

Make it usable

Call Avery to compare 406 and 422 Juniper — Thursday, 3 p.m.

Before you leave

Save a real date and time, then reopen and verify it.
slides.notes: Explain the difference between a note and a task. The note records history; the task schedules the next action. Complete the missed-call exercise next.

slides.title: Nurture needs a conversation
slides.lead: Compare two situations. Explain the evidence, next action, and review point.
slides.body:
Case A · Later timeline, still engaged

The buyer expects to move later and continues replying and discussing homes.

Case B · The record went quiet

The buyer has not responded recently. The record needs a review of what happened and what is due next.
slides.notes: Give everyone two minutes to write before discussing. Compare two contrasting responses, then explain the team’s actual nurture rule and why it applies. Do not invent a timeline, assume silence means nurture, or impose a follow-up standard beyond the doctrine’s first-week rule. There is no automatic grade. Review the evidence and preserve an owned next action.
slides.cue: What evidence changes your decision, and what still needs to happen?

activity.prompt: Compare the engaged, later-timeline buyer with the record that went quiet.

fields.label: For each case, what evidence would you need before moving this lead to nurture?

slides.lead: Only a request to compare homes is confirmed. The record says Appointment set.

What happened

Read the simulated record

slides.title: Where will you start tomorrow?
slides.lead: After training, apply this routine in your team’s Follow Up Boss account. For now, explain it here.
slides.body:
Due tasks

Review what you agreed to do and when.

New leads

Find the correct contact and read the history.

After each conversation

Update the stage, note, and dated next task.
slides.notes: Give 30 seconds without notes. Then ask partners to compare. Revisit only the missing item, not the entire lesson. This is a discussion of later real-work application, not an instruction to leave the session or update a client during class.

slides.title: Before your next client conversation
slides.lead: Write down when you will practice again.
slides.body:
After each conversation

Save the true stage, factual note, and dated next action before moving on.

With your coach

Review a real record together after the next relevant client conversation.
slides.notes: In live sessions, closing the session creates 24-hour recall, three-day fresh-case, and seven-day coach-review assignments. Confirm each agent’s named coach and session timezone. Agents see due work in Rep; the daily digest links to due or reviewable work. In self-paced study, arrange these checks with a coach. Without a relevant client opportunity, use a fresh fictional case and label real-work application not yet observed. Practice readiness is separate from quiz certification and activation.

resources:
Today’s workspace

Stay in your assigned TrueHQ live session. The People list is a reference walkthrough; the interactive exercises open inside fictional contacts. No separate Follow Up Boss account is needed for class.

Your own practice

Complete each opened activity on your own screen. Submit written answers here. For record exercises, save your changes and check your work here to send the result to your presenter. Each record exercise is a separate case.

Catch up

If the presenter moves on, finish your current activity and use Return to presenter. Unsubmitted writing stays private.

After class

Complete your 24-hour recall, three-day fresh case, and seven-day coaching review in Rep. Apply the routine in your team’s Follow Up Boss account after training. In self-paced study, arrange these checks with a coach.

What completion means

A record check verifies saved actions. The People-list walkthrough does not verify hands-on search. Observed practice, coach readiness, quiz certification, and activation remain separate.
